title.narrative: Joint SDG Fund thematic window Global Accelerator for Decent Work and Social Protection

description.narrative: The Global Accelerator on Jobs and Social Protection for Just Transitions (Global Accelerator) was launched in September 2021 by the UN Secretary General and promotes a job-rich recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as just ecological, technological, and societal transitions to more sustainable and inclusive economies and societies. The Global Accelerator will host a Technical Support Facility (TSF). The TSF brings together national and international expertise, including from the UN system as well as development and financial partners, building on or complementing the inter-agency work supported under the Joint SDG Fund to provide technical assistance to countries and facilitate their access to additional financial support, where appropriate. The Joint SDG Fund thematic window Global Accelerator for Decent Work and Social Protection is a multi-partner initiative established to address the significant socio-economic challenges faced by many countries, particularly in the wake of the pandemic, climate emergency, and other crises. The project focuses on social infrastructure, specifically social protection and welfare services policy, planning, and administration within the sector of social services (16xxx). The rationale behind this initiative is to bridge the "great finance divide" by mobilizing financing on a large scale to mitigate the devastating socio-economic hardship and job loss caused by these crises. Employment losses and reduced working hours have led to diminished incomes, exacerbated by the absence of adequate social protection systems in many countries, which has further stressed economically vulnerable households. The project aims to operationalize the Joint SDG Fund's Strategy for 2023-2026, Financing Catalytic Action for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It establishes a Thematic Window on Decent Jobs and Universal Social Protection (the Window) to support the implementation of the Global Accelerator on Jobs and Social Protection for Just Transitions in pathfinder countries. This window will address country priorities and foster greater collaboration among UN agencies and International Financial Institutions (IFIs) for dedicated funding rounds. The project builds on lessons learned from previous portfolios of investments by the Joint SDG Fund, notably "integrated policy solutions for social protection to leave no one behind" and "SDG financing". It aims to develop integrated and evidence-based national strategies and policies for social protection, employment, and just transitions. The project also focuses on integrated financing, combining domestic resources and international financial support. The initiative is supported by multiple UN entities, including DESA, UNFPA, DCO, UNICEF, EOSG, UN Women, ILO, WFP, IOM, WHO, Regional commissions, UNDP, and UNEP. The project is part of a larger effort to respond to the lack of fiscal space, with the objective of the Global Accelerator being to create 400 million jobs and extend social protection coverage to 4 billion people, although the pandemic has increased debt levels and weakened individual countries’ economic capacity to service and repay that debt.

These three interlinked pillars aim to increase the level and coordination of the multilateral system’s efforts to help countries create 400 million decent jobs, including in the green, digital and care economies, and to extend social protection coverage to the 4 billion people currently excluded. A joined-up effort of this scale and nature is critically needed to eradicate poverty and reduce inequalities, and thus pave the way for achieving the SDGs. Three complementary and mutually supportive areas of work are envisaged under the Global Accelerator: 1) the in-country development of integrated and coordinated employment and social protection policies and strategies that facilitate just transitions; 2) the establishment of national financing frameworks and the mobilization of public and private domestic and international resources to invest in universal social protection and inclusive, environment- and gender-responsive employment interventions with a view to creating quality jobs; and 3) the improvement of multilateral cooperation on jobs and social protection for just transitions, including with international financial institutions
